service_boundary: Represents Baseten's managed inference and training platform operated by Baseten Labs. The open-source packaging tooling it publishes and the models customers deploy remain separate boundaries.
regional_controls: Baseten documents multi-cloud capacity management across providers and regions, regional environments intended to satisfy data-residency requirements, private networking, and workload isolation. Specific region availability depends on the hosting option selected.
retention_controls: Baseten's terms make the customer the exclusive owner of its content, prohibit training on customer content, limit Baseten's own use to deidentified and aggregated statistics, and commit to destroying copies of customer content after a twenty-day retrieval window following termination.
routing: The platform provisions GPU capacity across clouds and regions and autoscales dedicated deployments; it is not a cross-provider model router and does not expose upstream provider selection.
customization: Dedicated deployment of open-source, fine-tuned, and custom models is a primary path, alongside supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning loops and training jobs on dedicated GPU clusters.
strengths: Hosted model APIs and dedicated deployment of customer-supplied models sit in one platform with a shared observability surface.
Terms are explicit that customer content is customer-owned, is not used for training, and is destroyed after a stated retrieval window.
Multi-cloud capacity management with regional environments and private networking addresses procurement and residency constraints directly.
tradeoffs: Region and capacity availability depend on the hosting option and provider mix rather than a single published region list.
The platform targets teams operating their own models; it is not a catalogue of third-party proprietary frontier models.
Anthropic Messages compatibility is documented as beta, so contract parity should be confirmed before relying on it.

response_integrity.note: No signature, attestation, or equivalent mechanism for verifying that a response arrived unaltered from the model appears in the API reference or the security documentation.
response_integrity.scope: Baseten Model APIs overview, for Baseten

upstream_disclosure.note: The terms state only that the hosting party "will, at its own expense, provide for the hosting of the applicable Baseten Products & Services"; the privacy policy does not address model inputs or outputs, and the trust centre's subprocessor list renders only by script.
upstream_disclosure.scope: Baseten terms and conditions, read for Baseten

credential_handling.note: Customer secrets used by deployed models are stored in a documented store: "store a Hugging Face access token as a secret named hf_access_token in Baseten's secret manager". Whether the store encrypts at rest is not stated.
credential_handling.scope: Baseten private Hugging Face model guide, for Baseten

cache_isolation.note: The runtime-caching page ("Cache is shared across every replica within a single deployment.") concerns model weights and build artefacts, not prompt caching; no page states how a prompt or prefix cache is scoped.
cache_isolation.scope: Baseten runtime-caching page, read for Baseten

vulnerability_disclosure.note: The public trust centre publishes a disclosure route: "If you believe you've discovered a security vulnerability in our services, please report it to security@baseten.co with details of your findings."

independent_audit.note: The operator's announcement states: "Baseten has completed a rigorous audit by Sensiba San Filippo LLP, a leading CPA firm, to achieve System and Organization Controls (SOC) 2 Type II certification." The public trust centre lists a Baseten Labs, Inc. SOC 2 Type 2 report behind a request-access control.
